newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ag min wants more food market protection.
newsitem.headline: Polish ag min wants more food market protection.

text.p: Poland's agriculture ministry wants to use the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) protective clause on food trade to reduce the country's food trade deficit in 1997, the minister, Jaroslaw Kalinowski, said on Monday.
Kalinowski told Reuters in an interview his ministry had prepared a list of goods which, after going through WTO-required procedures, could be protected by the government.

"Several days ago in the ministry we approved a list of goods...After presenting it to our foreign partners and after two months, possibly around September, we will be able to start using it," Kalinowski said.

"If we see that certain imported goods are cheaper than under the WTO agreement, we will be able to say that their exports are subsidised and raise the level of protection of our market," Kalinowski said.

He said the list was very comprehensive, from roses to poultry. Kalinowski added he expected Poland's food trade deficit this year would not be higher than in 1996 when it amounted to $1 billion against $476 million in 1995.
"I expect the food trade deficit this year will ease or at least not be higher than last year, mainly thanks to lower grain imports," he said.
Kalinowski added that grain imports in the first quarter of the year were about one million tonnes, two times smaller than in the same period last year.
